claims.statement: BIP 67 (Kerin, Rupp, de Vries) was assigned in 2015 and is recorded as Complete; it is a Specification in the Applications layer.

evidence.quote: Layer: Applications Title: Deterministic Pay-to-script-hash multi-signature addresses through public key sorting Authors: Thomas Kerin <me@thomaskerin.io> Jean-Pierre Rupp <root@haskoin.com> Ruben de Vries <ruben@rubensayshi.com> Status: Complete Type: Specification Assigned: 2015-02-08

claims.statement: BIP 48 (Fontaine) was assigned in 2020 and is recorded as Deployed.

evidence.quote: Title: Multi-Script Hierarchy for Multi-Sig Wallets Authors: Fontaine <dentondevelopment@protonmail.com> Status: Deployed Type: Specification Assigned: 2020-12-16

claims.statement: BIP 67 defines how the public keys are encoded and sorted, so that a given set of keys and required signatures always gives the same redeem script and P2SH address.

evidence.quote: It focuses on defining how the public keys must be encoded and sorted so that the redeem script and corresponding P2SH address are always the same for a given set of keys and number of required signatures.

claims.statement: BIP 67's authors note that the redeem script needs no particular key order or encoding, and count as many as 2(n!) standard redeem scripts for a key set and threshold, each with its own P2SH address.

evidence.quote: The redeem script does not require a particular ordering or encoding for public keys. This means that for a given set of keys and number of required signatures, there are as many as 2(n!) possible standard redeem scripts, each with its separate P2SH address.

claims.statement: The authors' motivation: compliant wallets always produce the same address for the same keys and threshold, which makes the account's transactions easier to recognize; for HD multisig wallets only the threshold and the participants' master public keys need sharing.

evidence.quote: compliant wallets will always produce the same P2SH address for the same given set of keys and required signature count, making it easier to recognize transactions involving that multi-signature account. This is particularly attractive for multisignature hierarchical-deterministic wallets, as less state is required to setup multi-signature accounts: only the number of required signatures and master public keys of participants need to be shared

claims.statement: The authors expect the convention to let someone other than a 2-of-3 wallet service recover the wallet without the service's help.

evidence.quote: Many wallet as a service providers use a 2of3 multi-signature schema where the user stores 1 of the keys (offline) as backup while using the other key for daily use and letting the service cosign his transactions. This standard will help in enabling a party other than the service provider to recover the wallet without any help from the service provider.

claims.statement: The redeem script is hashed as BIP 16 specifies to give the P2SH address.

claims.statement: Uncompressed keys are incompatible: an implementation should not compress them automatically, and an uncompressed key from a participant signals an incompatible implementation.

evidence.quote: Uncompressed keys are incompatible with this specification. A compatible implementation should not automatically compress keys. Receiving an uncompressed key from a multisig participant should be interpreted as a sign that the user has an incompatible implementation.

claims.statement: The authors note that a P2SH address reveals nothing about the script receiving the funds, and conclude that BIP 67 cannot be enforced as a network rule; doing so would also be a hard fork.

evidence.quote: P2SH addresses do not reveal information about the script that is receiving the funds. For this reason it is not technically possible to enforce this BIP as a rule on the network. Also, it would cause a hard fork.

claims.statement: The authors warn that if a group is not entirely compliant, a participant may derive an address the others do not recognize as part of their shared account.

evidence.quote: If a group of users were not entirely compliant, there is the possibility that a participant will derive an address that the others will not recognize as part of the common multisig account.

BIP 48 wallets inherently sort keys as BIP 67 describes, so every multisig address and script they make comes from sorted public keys.

evidence.quote: Any wallet that supports BIP48 inherently supports deterministic key sorting as per BIP67 so that all possible multi-signature addresses/scripts are derived from deterministically sorted public keys.

claims.statement: BIP 48's first four levels are hardened, and BIP 32 defines public derivation only for non-hardened children, so a master public key cannot give a cosigner's keys at a BIP 48 path; what a cosigner can share is the extended public key at the script-type level, below which change and index use public derivation.

evidence.quote: m / purpose' / coin_type' / account' / script_type' / change / address_index h or ' in the path indicates that BIP32 hardened derivation is used.
Public derivation is used at this level.
It is only defined for non-hardened child keys.

claims.statement: Each cosigner derives keys under BIP 48's hierarchy from their own seed; for each address the keys sorted are the cosigners' keys at that change and index, so one cosigner's place in the script can differ from one address to the next.

evidence.quote: Any wallet that supports BIP48 inherently supports deterministic key sorting as per BIP67 so that all possible multi-signature addresses/scripts are derived from deterministically sorted public keys.
Addresses are numbered from index 0 in sequentially increasing manner. This number is used as child index in BIP32 derivation.

claims.statement: BIP 48 writes down the existing industry practice of m/48' paths for multisig wallets, and lets future script types be appended without a new BIP.

evidence.quote: The motivation of this BIP is to define the existing industry wide practice of utilizing m/48' derivation paths in hierarchical deterministic multi-sig wallets so that other developers may benefit from a standard. This BIP allows for future script types to easily be appended to the specification so that a new BIP is not required for every future script type.

claims.statement: BIP 48 paths are m / purpose' / coin_type' / account' / script_type' / change / address_index, with purpose 48' and coin type 0 for mainnet or 1 for testnet; an apostrophe marks hardened derivation.
